rationale: The codebase already has working LLM-provider clients for both Claude Code and Codex CLIs; this is an enrichment (add auto-detection + defaulting glue to two existing, well-understood resolution points) rather than an investigation into unknown behavior.

queries.intent: Locate how the bookstore CLI/MCP server resolves its LLM configuration today
Confirm whether an ai-parrot client already wraps the Claude Agent SDK / Claude Code CLI credentials

params.pattern: Claude Agent SDK client Claude Code credentials

queries.intent: Read the full shared LLM-resolution helper to confirm the exact degraded-mode contract and env vars
Verify there is no hardcoded Gemini default anywhere in wiki/bookstore code (only illustrative doc examples)
Find the exact source of the warning the requester hit ("No LLM configured for the bookstore")

params.pattern: No LLM configured for the bookstore

queries.intent: Read the Bookstore/_NullAdapter degraded-mode design to understand the philosophy being changed
Find wikitoolkit's own model-resolution points (WIKI_MODEL / WIKI_LIGHTWEIGHT_MODEL / WIKI_EXTRACT_LLM) in wiki/cli.py
Check whether an existing coding-agent CLI detector (wiki/coding_agents.py) can be reused for LLM-provider defaulting
Enumerate every registered parrot.clients entry point to confirm Claude Code and Codex both already have first-class LLMFactory providers
Confirm ClaudeAgentClient/OpenAICodexClient use a lazy, cheap-to-check SDK import guard rather than an eager subprocess/network call
Find a documented cheap/deterministic model id for each provider (Haiku for Claude, an equivalent for Codex)
Confirm the env-var-default table in the shipped docs so the proposal's baseline claim ("no default = none, not Gemini") is documented, not just code-derived

expected_findings: Neither bookstore nor wikitoolkit hardcodes a default LLM provider today — unset env vars mean fully degraded mode, by design.
ClaudeAgentClient (claude-agent/claude-code) and OpenAICodexClient (codex-agent/openai-codex/codex-code) are already registered LLMFactory providers — no new client code is needed.
Both clients guard the actual SDK import behind a lazy, exception-safe helper, which is the right primitive to build safe-execution detection on top of.
wiki/coding_agents.py is a precedent for CLI-name dispatch (codex/claude/gemini) but installs wiki hooks, not LLM defaults — not directly reusable, but confirms the three CLI names to detect.
